paragraphs: Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother.

(a) He is the unqualified Chananyah in a baraita, as in Mi SheHotziuhu, Eruvin 43a. So Yuchasin writes in the sequence of generations under R. Yehoshua ben Chananyah. He was a Levite: Rashi, Berakhot 63b, beginning.

(b) He went to Babylonia, to Nehar Pekod, to intercalate the year. Rabbi sent him three letters through R. Yitzchak and R. Natan. Yuchasin writes “R. Yitzchak and R. Natan were with him,” but this is not so: “through” means by their agency he sent the three letters. One letter said, “To the holiness of Chananyah”: he praised him and warned him not to intercalate outside the Land, because he was holy and should not act unlawfully. One said, “The kids you left have become he-goats”—meaning, do not say that because you left no one your equal in the Land of Israel, you may intercalate abroad. One said, “If you do not accept, go to the wilderness of the thornbush; you shall slaughter, and Nechunyon shall sprinkle”—meaning that it would be like building an altar abroad and offering on it. He read the first and honored them, R. Yitzchak and R. Natan; he read the second and honored them. At the third he wished to disparage them. They said, “You cannot, for you have already honored them.” R. Yitzchak rose and read in the Torah, “These are Chananyah's appointed seasons”—since he intercalated abroad, these were only Chananyah's seasons. R. Natan rose and completed: “For from Babylonia shall Torah go forth, and the word of the Lord from Nehar Pekod.” They told him, “For from Zion shall Torah go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.” He went to complain against them before R. Yehudah ben Beteira at Nisibis. He told him, “Rabbi acted well, for one should not intercalate abroad”: Jerusalem Sanhedrin, chapter 1, halakhah 2; Nedarim, chapter 6, halakhah 8 in the checked edition. Babylonian HaRoeh, Berakhot 63: when Chanina, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, went into exile, he intercalated years and fixed months outside the Land. They sent two Torah scholars after him: R. Yosi ben Kipper and Zekharyah ben Kevutal's grandson. He asked why they had come. They said, “We came to study Torah.” He proclaimed, “These men are the generation's great men, etc.” He began declaring impure while they declared pure. He proclaimed, “These men are worthless, etc.” They told him, “You have already built and cannot demolish.” He asked why they were declaring pure. They answered, “Because you intercalate abroad.” He said, “But Akiva ben Yosef intercalated abroad!” They answered, “R. Akiva left no one his equal in the Land of Israel.” He said, “I too left no one my equal there.” They replied, “The kids you left have become he-goats. They sent me to you: if you do not obey them, you will be under a ban.” Yuchasin writes that Rabban Gamliel sent two Torah scholars.

(c) He issued a ruling in Rabban Gamliel's and his uncle R. Yehoshua's time. Niddah 24b: a woman miscarried a snake-like form. Chanina, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, ruled that its mother was impure through childbirth. R. Yosef went—so too in the new Talmud editions, but we have not found an R. Yosef in their time; Yuchasin writes R. Yosi HaGelili—and related the matter before Rabban Gamliel. Rabban Gamliel sent to R. Yehoshua, “Lead your nephew”—come with him. As they walked, R. Chanina's daughter-in-law came out to meet R. Yehoshua. She asked, “My teacher, what of a woman who miscarries something like a snake?” He answered, “Its mother is pure.” She said, “But my mother-in-law told me in your name that its mother is impure!” He asked, “For what reason?” The reason given was that its eyeball is round like a human’s. Through her words R. Yehoshua remembered. He sent Rabban Gamliel: “Chanina ruled from my own mouth.” Abaye said: learn from this that a scholar who states a teaching should state its reason, so that when reminded, he remembers.

(d) “Justice, justice shall you pursue”: follow R. Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, into exile—Sanhedrin 32b. Ein Yaakov has a scribal error, which Nachalat Shimoni did not notice. Yuchasin, in the sequence of generations after the priests' section, writes: Sifrei, Reeh, says that R. Yehudah ben Beteira, R. Matya ben Cheresh, R. Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, and R. Yonatan tore their clothes when they left the Land, since dwelling in the Land of Israel equals all the commandments. Apparently these men were not together; rather, each left the Land separately: R. Yehudah ben Beteira to Babylonia, to Nisibis; R. Matya ben Cheresh to Rome; R. Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, into exile. It was taught: “Chananyah says: Beit Shammai says”—Beitzah, chapter 2, 17b. Ketubot 79b has Chananyah, son of Yoshiyah's brother; perhaps a scribal error for R. Yehoshua. Chullin 47b: R. Chananyah fell ill, and R. Natan and the generation's great men visited him. Chagigah 10a: R. Eliezer says; R. Yehoshua says; R. Yitzchak says; Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, says. End of chapter 1 of Sukkah: “When I went into exile”—Rashi: to intercalate the year, as in HaRoeh—“and when I came to R. Yehoshua, my father's brother.” Kohelet Midrash, on “All things are wearying”: the sectarians of Kefar Nachum bewitched him, and he rode a donkey on the Sabbath. His uncle R. Yehoshua treated him; he went down to Babylonia and died there. There, in the interpretation of “good” on “I find [more bitter than death],” this is R. Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother. R. Elazar ben Azaryah, in R. Elazar HaModai's name: Shevuot 35b. R. Achiya, his colleague; and R. Dostai son of R. Yannai.
